value.body: A science degree in electronic circuits and devices: analog and digital electronics, semiconductor devices, microprocessors and microcontrollers, communication and instrumentation, with substantial lab work. It is usually studied with Physics, Mathematics or Computer Science. It leads to technical and service roles in the electronics industry, an M.Sc, or an MCA.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 years for Honours / Honours with Research under the UGC four-year UG framework (NEP 2020)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in the science stream with Physics and Mathematics. Central universities admit through CUET-UG; many state universities and colleges admit on Class 12 merit or a state test. Some offer Electronics only as one subject in a combination (for example Physics, Electronics and Mathematics).

value.title: At a glance
items: Fewer colleges offer it than B.Sc Physics or Chemistry.
Entry jobs are often in testing, servicing and manufacturing; design roles usually go to B.Tech or M.Sc graduates.
Common next steps are an M.Sc Electronics or an MCA.
Government options include technical-assistant posts at science organisations and graduate-level exams.
